mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The Sun appears to move east to west each day because Earth revolves around the Sun.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Earth rotates anticlockwise when viewed from above either the North Pole or the South Pole.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The Sun's daily east-to-west motion makes Earth rotate from west to east.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Earth's rotation explains only the Sun's apparent daily motion, not the Moon's or stars'.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth rotates on its own axis in about 24 hours; when viewed from Earth, that west-to-east rotation makes the Sun appear to rise in the east, move across the sky, and set in the west. Earth's west-to-east rotation changes the observer's direction in space, producing the Sun's apparent east-to-west motion. The learner correctly applies this rule: Earth rotates on its own axis in about 24 hours; when viewed from Earth, that west-to-east rotation makes the Sun appear to rise in the east, move across the sky, and set in the west. The Sun itself travels from East to West across a still Earth each day.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky.
